cec-held.title: Կայացած ընտրություններ (ընտրացանկ), 1 սեպտեմբերի 1997թ. էջում, arquivo.pt snapshot of 16 February 2023
cec-held.note: The commission's site (cecnkr.am, offline since 2023) listed every election it held under 'Կայացած': presidential elections from 24 November 1996, National Assembly elections from 28 December 1991 with by-elections from 2012, local self-government elections from 27 September 1998, and referendums from 10 December 1991. Read from the 16 February 2023 arquivo.pt capture of the page on the 1997 presidential election.

cec-1996.title: ԼՂՀ Նախագահի ընտրություն, 24 նոյեմբերի 1996թ.
cec-1996.note: Final result of the first presidential election: 8 district (city) commissions, 171 precinct commissions, 89,733 voters on the lists, 70,052 voting; Robert Kocharyan elected with 60,241 votes. arquivo.pt capture of 16 February 2023.

cec-1997.title: ԼՂՀ Նախագահի արտահերթ ընտրություն, 1 սեպտեմբերի 1997թ.
cec-1997.note: Final result of the early presidential election called after Robert Kocharyan became Prime Minister of Armenia: 90,137 voters on the lists, 76,257 voting; Arkadi Ghukasyan elected with 65,933 votes. arquivo.pt capture of 16 February 2023.

cec-ref2017.title: Ամփոփվել են հանրաքվեի վերջնական արդյունքները (23.02.2017)
cec-ref2017.note: Final result of the 20 February 2017 constitutional referendum: 103,818 entitled to vote, 79,428 voting, 69,570 for and 7,686 against. arquivo.pt capture of 16 February 2023.

constitution-2017.title: The Constitution of the Republic of Artsakh (2017)
constitution-2017.note: English text on the National Assembly's site (nankr.am), arquivo.pt capture of 7 December 2023. Arts. 7 and 48 (suffrage), 88-90 (President: five-year term, absolute majority with a second round on the fourteenth day, extraordinary elections), 107-109 (National Assembly of 27 to 33 deputies, proportional, five-year term, elected with the President), 150 (council of elders and head of community, five-year term), 162 (referendums), 168 (President elected by the National Assembly in the transition), 171 (majoritarian by-elections), 174 (local bodies elected under the 2006 Constitution).

mfa-declaration.title: Declaration on Proclamation of the Nagorno Karabakh Republic (2 September 1991)
mfa-declaration.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Nagorno-Karabakh Republic
mfa-declaration.note: Text of the declaration adopted by the joint session of the Nagorno Karabakh Oblast and Shahumyan regional councils on 2 September 1991, on the Foreign Ministry's site (nkr.am), arquivo.pt capture of 17 June 2017.

president-expresidents.title: Ex-Presidents
president-expresidents.publisher: Office of the President of the Nagorno Karabagh Republic
president-expresidents.note: Biographies of Robert Kocharyan (elected by the Supreme Council on 24 December 1994, by popular vote in November 1996), Arkadi Ghukasyan (early election of September 1997, re-elected 11 August 2002), and Bako Sahakyan (President from 7 September 2007). arquivo.pt capture of 22 January 2022.

president-statepower.title: State Power
president-statepower.publisher: Office of the President of the Nagorno Karabagh Republic
president-statepower.note: President elected for five years; National Assembly of 33 deputies elected for five years (11 by majority vote, 22 by proportional representation, as for the 2015 election); seven regions and the capital Stepanakert. arquivo.pt capture of 22 January 2022.

na-home.title: Ազգային ժողով, գլխավոր էջ (լուրեր, սեպտեմբեր-նոյեմբեր 2023)
na-home.note: News of the special sitting of 9 September 2023 at which the National Assembly elected Samvel Shahramanyan President, and of his inauguration the same day; the latest item is dated 15 November 2023. arquivo.pt capture of 7 December 2023.

classes.name: Ազգային ժողովի ընտրություններ (1991-1995: Գերագույն խորհուրդ)
classes.finest_note: The commission's pages are lost but for the 1996 and 1997 presidential results; no file with results by constituency or precinct survives in a reachable archive.
classes.note: The Supreme Council elected on 28 December 1991 gave way to a National Assembly of 33 deputies, elected for five years from 1995. Deputies were first elected by majority vote in single-member constituencies and later under a mixed system (11 constituency and 22 national list seats in 2015); the 2017 Constitution made the Assembly fully proportional (27 to 33 deputies) and set its regular election on the same day as the President's, first held on 31 March 2020.

access.evidence: The commission's site gave a page for each National Assembly election from 1991 to 2020; the site has been offline since 2023 and arquivo.pt holds only its 1996 and 1997 presidential pages and the 2017 referendum result

dates.note: Supreme Council of the first convocation, elected eighteen days after the independence referendum.
First National Assembly, 33 deputies.
11 single-member constituencies and 22 national list seats.
First election under the 2017 Constitution: one national list contest for 33 seats, held with the presidential election.

classes.name: Ազգային ժողովի լրացուցիչ ընտրություններ
classes.note: A vacant constituency seat went to a by-election in its constituency; the 2017 Constitution kept them for the deputies elected by majority vote in 2015 (art. 171). The commission lists five, from 2012 to 2018.

access.evidence: Pages for the 2012, 2017, and 2018 by-elections, offline since 2023 and not in a reachable archive

dates.note: Held with the constitutional referendum.
Date as the commission lists it.

classes.name: Հանրապետության Նախագահի ընտրություններ
classes.finest_note: National totals survive for 1996 and 1997 on the commission's archived pages; 1996 was counted by 8 district (city) and 171 precinct commissions.
classes.note: Elected by popular vote for five years from 1996, at most two terms; a candidate needs more than half of the votes cast, failing which the top two meet in a second round on the fourteenth day (2017 Constitution art. 89). Vacancies bring an extraordinary election (art. 90), as in 1997; in 1994, 2017, and 2023 the legislature chose the President instead (see the indirect class).

cadence.runoff_rule: Top two on the fourteenth day after the first round

access.evidence: A page for each presidential election; the 1996 and 1997 pages survive at arquivo.pt with national totals

dates.quote: 1996թ. օգոստոսի 29-ին ԼՂՀ Ազգային ժողովը որոշում է ընդունել նոյեմբերի 24-ին անցկացնել ԼՂՀ Նախագահի առաջին ընտրությունը

classes.note: The Supreme Council elected the first President in December 1994. Under art. 168 of the 2017 Constitution the National Assembly elected the President for the transition to 2020, and on 9 September 2023 it elected Samvel Shahramanyan after Arayik Harutyunyan resigned.
